title: USB status LED
brief: A red LED shows that a board has USB power. Run it from the 5 V supply through one resistor so it carries 8 to 12 mA (the red LED drops about 1.9 V near 10 mA, as in First light), with the resistor at no more than half its ¼ W rating. Pick the resistor from the E12 series, predict the current and the resistor's power, build it, run it and measure both.

spec.how: Meter in series with the LED (the A and W tool on the LED)
spec.note: A real meter on its mA range adds a few to ten ohms of shunt and fuse (burden voltage) and reads 1–3 % less; tier 1 ignores it.

spec.quantity: Resistor power, against its ¼ W rating
spec.how: The A and W tool on the resistor: its power as a share of 250 mW

tiers.title: Supply range and tolerance
modifiers: USB 2.0 §7.2.2 and Table 7-7 allow 4.75 to 5.25 V at a high-power port.
The resistor is ±5 %: the current must stay in 8 to 12 mA at every corner.

tiers.title: The LED's forward-voltage spread
modifiers: A red LED specified at 1.8 to 2.2 V (spread to be cited): the current must stay in 8 to 12 mA at every corner. No 5 % E12 value does it; a 1 % E96 part does.
